page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Running head at top with page number at top left. Continuation paragraph at top, then a rule ornament, then centred chapter heading, italic title, thesis number, and the body paragraph with a large initial. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: tur duratio, atque omne adeò continuum, qua continuum, incipit in ultimo momento sui non esse, & definit in primo sui non esse: nam continuum non habet primum & ultimum sui esse. Si existentia tamen spectetur, non ut continua, sed ut existentia, incipit in primo & definit in ultimo sui esse, si sit permanens: At si sit successiva, incipit in ultimo sui non esse, & definit in primo sui non esse, sive consideretur ut existentia, sive ut continua.
main_text.head: CAP. XXII.
main_text.p: Dictum est de affectionibus Simplicibus; sequuntur Conjunctae, quae non singulae seorsim, sed ambae simul acceptae, de Ente praedicantur disjunctive. Huc pertinent primo totum & pars, causa & causatum, subjectum & adjunctum, quę Logica à Metaphysica mutuatur; deinde necessitas & contingentia, potentia & actus, perfectum & imperfectum: Non enim omne Ens totum quiddam est, nec etiam omne Ens pars est: sed Ens in totum & partem dividitur, ita ut quodlibet Ens dici possit aut totum aut pars, & sic de cae-teris.

page.notes: The first letter of the body paragraph is a large woodcut-style initial, read as "D" and joined to "ictum". The printed "Iĉtum" is read as "Dictum". The word "caeteris" is split at the line end as "cae-" / "teris" and is joined here with its printed hyphen. Thesis number "THESIS I." is set in spaced capitals; it is given as a paragraph because the guidelines treat numbered theses as paragraphs. The small mark at the foot and the faint watermark at the lower right are not printed text and are left out.
